svg.title: Recommended population order, following the thesis's own work-backwards method
svg.desc: Seven numbered steps in sequence. Steps one to four populate domains directly: the Interaction Model with the properties of the sonic and visual spaces; the Capability Model with a small set of deliberately discriminating user profiles; the Inventory with media elements; and then the Application Model, hand-populated by hand as a single concrete board rendered for one user, forming a fixed point. Step five is marked as the pivot: working backwards from that fixed point to derive what would have caused it, producing the Composition Model's rule sets as a derivation rather than a guess. Steps six and seven then build the Render Model to perform that derivation automatically, and the Adaptation layer to select among alternatives driven by capability. A note records that this replicates the method used in the Render Model note, which began from a hand-built Google Maps rendering and worked backwards.
svg.text: Populate the target first, then work backwards
Interaction Model
sonic and visual properties; zero dependencies
Capability Model
few profiles, chosen so selection discriminates
Inventory
media elements, populated but inert
Application Model, by hand
one board, one user, sonic space:
the fixed point, and the first thing that can be heard
Work backwards
what would have caused that population?
rule sets derived, not guessed
Render Model
does step 5 automatically; now a bridge is worth building
Adaptation
selects alternatives, driven by capability
The method is the thesis's own
"I start with an arbitrary concrete Application
Model of the rendered content using the Google
Maps example again, and then work backwards to
identify what would cause that Application Model
to be populated in this way."
Notes on The Render Model, Introduction
A hand-populated target needs no bridges:
it is asserted, not derived. That is what
sidesteps the dependency problem entirely.
Risk, recorded: the method was built for a static
document. Tetris is change, not snapshots, so the
fixed point may need to be a short sequence.
